parity_risks.note: A NULL join key matches nothing, so a target row with a NULL REGION or PERIOD leaves on the L anchor, which is wired to nothing, and never reaches the J stream. An inner join on `=` keeps that behaviour; a join written with IS NOT DISTINCT FROM would not. That is also why REGION and PERIOD are declared NOT NULL on this stream.

The join is many-to-many on (REGION, PERIOD): every target row is paired with every actual line of its key, so a key with two actual lines carries its TARGET twice. The fan-out is Alteryx's own behaviour and the golden data keeps it; the downstream Sum therefore counts a target once per actual line, and a translation that pre-aggregated the actuals before joining would disagree.

Key comparison is exact and case-sensitive -- no trimming, no case folding. Right_REGION and Right_PERIOD are deselected, so the stream carries the left side's key columns only, which on a matched row are equal to the right side's anyway.
